text: Writing init, repr, and eq by hand for every simple data class gets tedious — dataclasses do it for you.
Just add the dataclass decorator and list your fields with type hints, and Python generates the boilerplate.
You get a constructor, a readable repr, and value-based equality, all for free.
[chuckle] So printing a product shows a clean summary, and two equal products compare as equal automatically.
[sniff] For mutable defaults like lists, you use field with default_factory, avoiding a classic shared-state bug.
Each product gets its own fresh tags list, so appending to one never affects another.
[sigh] You can also make a dataclass frozen, turning it into an immutable, read-only object.
A frozen point can't be changed after creation, which makes it safe to use as a dictionary key.
[groan] Dataclasses cut dozens of lines down to a handful — they're the modern default for data-holding classes.
